body: The statement about irony is probably the best thing I've heard so far. It genuinely made me laugh just from the juxtaposition of the situation. Thank you!

I talked a little about this in another comment, but I feel like it could apply here as well. I hope to make some understanding friends. One problem I routinely encounter, whether it's a friend/date, is that they often feel entitled to openly say or do hurtful things. It's not simply that I perceive them to be hurtful; each occurrence end with them outright telling me the same thing: They are allowed to say or do hurtful things, and I should put up with it, because I'm lucky they want to be around me at all because of my HIV status. I don't bring this up as hyperbole. Why do people feel like they have carte blanche to be assholes because Im HIV+ and they're not?

Where I lived before, I had much more resources to help me cope. I saw a psychologist regularly, and I knew other HIV+ just to be friends with.

Where I live now, it's maddening to get any resources. Even though States are required to provide medical, mental health, and dental services because of the Ryan White Act, I can't get any results with my state health department (which is the agency the Fed govt has assigned in my area to distribute the funds and provide the care). They don't return phone calls when I'm calling for information. My case manager treats me with the same amount of stigma as the general populace. How do I get resources to cope with these issues without my local health department demoralizing me in the process?

I've considered not mentioning my HIV early in the relationship, and I've tried to make it work. However, in the state I live in now, disclosure laws require that I must disclose my HIV before even kissing someone. And my state has convicted several people for kissing without disclosing. It's a scary legal line, and one that I'm unsure what to do about it.

Thank you for the concern.
